*Discrete commands vs continuous intents.* If the sim must log, validate, save or replay it, it is a command (examples; each type's owner GDD is authoritative: Controller `set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, `toggle_beam`; Interaction `begin_cut` (module salvage, V8), `begin_patch`, `cancel_channel`, `pickup`, `drop`, `set_switch`, `field_check`; Modular Ship Assembly `begin_weld` (declared by Interaction, registered by Assembly), `begin_seam_cut`, `install_module` and the `SYSTEM`-only completions `weld` / `seam_cut` (registry: `assembly_commands`; there is no `remove_module` — it is reserved and unregistered, and V8 salvage is the only removal); Suit `equip_tool` (its only type); Web Map & Transit `pod_hop`, `berth`, `unberth` and the `SYSTEM`-only `pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`, `berth_step`, `web_reconcile` (registry: `web_commands`). `interact` is an input action, not a command type, and `use_item` has no owner and is not a command *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system, suit-and-equipment, modular-ship-assembly and web-map-and-transit)*). What the stick is doing *right now* is an intent: intents are commands too, but a type may declare `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` — coalescing happens at admission over the unfrozen queue, keyed `(type, actor, issuer_peer)`, the older command becoming `Superseded` — and the input adapter sends one only when the quantised value changes — a few per second, never one per tick. Edge-triggered inputs (press, release, confirm) must declare `coalesce = NONE` or taps are lost. Movement integration runs inside the sim: Body's `body.integrate` hook (divisor 1, P3) reads the current intent and integrates ship-local kinematics (CR-13), so a move intent takes effect one tick after it is submitted, like every command; there is no physics-side integration at MVP, and position ownership is settled (Body owns it; the Controller owns intent and facing) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` every command is round-tripped through serialization before dispatch, even locally; one that cannot survive is a violation (CR-19). **Submit is fire-and-forget and never calls back**: `submit()` returns nothing and invokes no callback, handler or subscriber, so it is safe to call from any handler, hook or result handler; its only outcome is one result record appended to the kernel's result buffer (CR-5), delivered at the next flush and identified by `result_id` — a remote issuer could never get a synchronous answer, so the local one doesn't either *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `submit()` takes the optional `correlation` and returns nothing, not even a receipt: the caller learns the outcome only from the result record, which carries its `correlation` back, so "fire-and-forget" is literally true and `seq` stays the kernel's. The API shape is `submit(type, payload, actor = none, correlation = 0)` on an `INPUT_SURFACE` handle and `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key = none)` for hooks (a hook needs no correlation: it never receives a result); `submit_system` and `has_pending` are methods of the `HookContext` and `ApplyContext` the kernel passes in, plus the test ingress, never a free function, and the `INPUT_SURFACE` submit right is a capability handle issued only in `BOOTING`, separate from subscribing in that class *(Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0002 GDD sync)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*.

-**Payload whitelist** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. 'Plain' is a recursive `Variant.Type` whitelist checked at admission: `NIL`, `BOOL`, `INT`, `FLOAT` (finite only — `NaN` and `±inf` are `MALFORMED`; the same finite check applies to **each component of a `VECTOR2` and each element of `PackedFloat32Array`, `PackedFloat64Array` and `PackedVector2Array`**, which the walk visits in O(n) bounded by `MAX_PAYLOAD` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `STRING`, `STRING_NAME`, `VECTOR2`, `VECTOR2I`, the `Packed{Byte,Int32,Int64,Float32,Float64,String,Vector2}Array` types, and `ARRAY`/`DICTIONARY` of the same, to a depth cap `PAYLOAD_MAX_DEPTH` = 8 (which also rejects a self-containing container). Dictionary keys must be `INT`, `STRING` or `STRING_NAME` and **all keys of one dictionary must share one type** (mixed keys have no canonical order, D.12). Anything else — an `Object`, `NodePath`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, a non-whitelisted `Variant.Type`, a non-finite float, a depth-9 nesting, mixed dictionary keys — is `MALFORMED`; the size bound is measured as `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size()` after the walk passes. Immediate *acknowledgement* (a tool sound, a hand animation, a linear progress bar starting) is presentation's job and happens in the same frame; the sim confirms on the next tick. The latency bounds are stated once, in Game Feel and D.4.

+**Payload whitelist** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. 'Plain' is a recursive `Variant.Type` whitelist checked at admission: `NIL`, `BOOL`, `INT`, `FLOAT` (finite only — `NaN` and `±inf` are `MALFORMED`; the same finite check applies to **each component of a `VECTOR2` and each element of `PackedFloat32Array`, `PackedFloat64Array` and `PackedVector2Array`**, which the walk visits in O(n) bounded by `MAX_PAYLOAD` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `STRING`, `STRING_NAME`, `VECTOR2`, `VECTOR2I`, the `Packed{Byte,Int32,Int64,Float32,Float64,String,Vector2}Array` types, and `ARRAY`/`DICTIONARY` of the same, to a depth cap `PAYLOAD_MAX_DEPTH` = 8 (which also rejects a self-containing container). Dictionary keys must be `INT`, `STRING` or `STRING_NAME` and **all keys of one dictionary must share one type** (mixed keys have no canonical order, D.12). Anything else — an `Object`, `NodePath`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, a non-whitelisted `Variant.Type`, a non-finite float, a depth-9 nesting, mixed dictionary keys — is `MALFORMED`; the size bound is measured as `var_to_bytes(payload).size()` after the walk passes. Immediate *acknowledgement* (a tool sound, a hand animation, a linear progress bar starting) is presentation's job and happens in the same frame; the sim confirms on the next tick. The latency bounds are stated once, in Game Feel and D.4.

**CR-5. Command lifecycle and the exactly-one-result guarantee.** Every command reaches exactly one terminal state and emits exactly one result record (identified by `result_id`; delivered to its issuer unless it is `SYSTEM`-origin, see Result identity and delivery below). Stages: *Issued* → *Admission* (kernel state accepts commands; type registered; **origin allowed for the type — known at admission, so rejected there**; queue not full; `seq` not a duplicate — gaps are accepted and counted, not rejected; issuer rate limit; payload plain) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0002 GDD sync: the normative admission order is: stamp `submission_id` and `seq`; resolve the type; kernel state (`PAUSED` unless the type is `allowed_when_paused`); origin; duplicate `seq`; rate limit; payload (whitelist walk, size, schema); coalescing; queue capacity. An unknown type submitted while `PAUSED` is therefore `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, and capacity is checked after coalescing because a supersession can free room. A `Superseded` tombstone frees its `QUEUE_CAPACITY` and `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` count at once, and the queue-flush `Dropped(RELOAD|SHUTDOWN|FAULTED)` results are the existing CR-16 behaviour)* → *Queued* → *Authority check* in P2 (origin re-checked as a defence in depth; if the type declares `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, the binding table says the issuer controls the key `(actor_source, actor)` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; age ≤ the type's `max_age_ticks`) → *Validate* (owner's side-effect-free `validate(cmd, views, ctx)`: it reports through `ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)` — a domain reason — and ends with `return ctx.complete()`; its return value carries no outcome, CR-19(a)/(b)) → *Apply* (`apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, ending with `return ctx.complete()`; infallible by contract once validate passed, CR-9) → terminal: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3)*

**CR-7. Authority model (behaviour).** The host is the sole authority: only a `HOST` kernel ticks and applies; a `MIRROR` never applies. Each command type's owner declares `allowed_origins ⊆ {PLAYER, SYSTEM}` and `actor_binding ∈ {NONE, OWNED_BY_ISSUER}` — both mandatory (CR-6) — and `allowed_origins` is checked at admission, with a P2 re-check as defence in depth. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A type with `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` also declares **`actor_source`**: the `block_id` of the registered binding source whose ID space its `actor` belongs to (`body.state` for every avatar-acting type, `emitter.state` for `toggle_beam`). The P2 authority check passes iff `(actor_source(type), actor) ∈ half_b[PlayerId(issuer_peer)]`. So an actor and a beam with the same number can never stand in for each other. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* `SYSTEM` commands never arrive from a network; remote ingress always stamps `PLAYER`. The kernel holds a **binding table** — `peer_id → PlayerId` and `PlayerId → {(source block_id, entity_id)}` — as identity data, not domain state; the table has two halves with different lifetimes *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6 (user delegated all remaining calls): the kernel owns the rebuild; closes Body Open Question 30)*. **(a) `peer_id → PlayerId`** is session state: it is mutated only through a host-only API called by the session owner (`request_bind_seat(peer_id, player_id)` and `request_unbind_seat(peer_id)`, CR-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0002 GDD sync)* (a boot step in MVP: `HOST_PEER_ID` 1 → PlayerId 1; Co-op Session in VS-B), and a restore, a death restart or a new game never touches it and never resets any issuer's `seq` or `last_seq`. **(b) `PlayerId → {(source block_id, entity_id)}`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* is derived from saved state and is never saved: **the kernel rebuilds it itself as the last step of every pass through `LOADING`** (`request_restore` and `request_new_game` alike), after the last `post_restore()` and the K-4 hash check and before the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition. The rebuild clears half (b) entirely, then calls each registered **binding source** (CR-6, CR-8) in ascending `block_id` order — with `ctx`, as a pure read of its owner's block, under no `WriteScope`, ending `return ctx.complete()` — which delivers `[(player_id, entity_id)]` in ascending order through `ctx.put`, and binds every pair under the source's own `block_id`: each delivered `(player_id, entity_id)` is stored as `player_id → (source_block_id, entity_id)`. Entity IDs are block-local (CR-8: each owner allocates from its own counter and the kernel allocates none), so the key always carries the source. Equal numbers from two sources (Body actor 1 and Emitter beam 1) are two different keys and never conflict. A key `(source_block_id, entity_id)` delivered for two different PlayerIds, or the same triple `(player_id, source_block_id, entity_id)` delivered twice, is `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT`. A source that reports `ctx.fault` or returns without the sentinel is that source's fault. Either one takes `LOADING → FAULTED` naming the source. **CR-9. Write discipline and atomicity.** A block is written only by its owner's mutators, and only inside a `WriteScope` the kernel issues during P2 apply or P3 step; outside those phases a mutator is refused in every build (no write, no dirty key), increments `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Cross-block commands** (weld, cut, module install, pod hop) call *public mutators* other owners explicitly publish; the kernel guarantees the whole `apply` is atomic against every other command, hook and snapshot, followed by one notification batch. **Failure model: validate-then-apply, no rollback.** `validate` proves everything through read-only queries (for weld, the Graph's pure join-validation query); `apply` is infallible by contract; a failure inside `apply` — reported through the fault channel, never by throwing or asserting (CR-19) — is a defect that moves the kernel to `FAULTED` (C.2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Copy-on-write rollback rejected for MVP cost; event sourcing rejected as primary store — the kernel keeps a bounded command log for diagnostics and replay tests only.)* Step hooks affect other systems by (a) a published unconditional mutator (a horror writing a footprint into the Graph's footprint channel) or (b) a `SYSTEM`-origin command processed at T+1 when the target may reject. The kernel enforces *phase*; "only declared callers call declared mutators" is enforced by lint and the control manifest. → ADR

- **If one issuer's pending count reaches `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` (256)**: that issuer's next submit is rejected `QUEUE_FULL`; all other issuers are unaffected. Supersession still works for that issuer (it frees a slot before the capacity check).

- **If the global pending count reaches `QUEUE_CAPACITY` (1024)**: every issuer's next submit, including the local player's and `SYSTEM` submits from hooks, is rejected `QUEUE_FULL`; the hook receives no result (`SYSTEM` results go to the log only) and must tolerate rejection and read the outcome from state (CR-9 owner rule; path (b) targets may reject anyway). 150	**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. 151	
152	**The token check.** The kernel keeps one `CompletionToken` per context object. `complete()` sets `completed = true`, writes the current epoch into the token and returns it. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. Anything else, including `null`, a type default or a token kept from an earlier call, is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` (or, for a handler or a view callable, a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic without a fault). The check does not depend on what an aborted call returns (Verification 1). One hole is closed by rule: an owner that aborted *after* `complete()` ran would read as success, so `return ctx.complete()` is the **last statement** and nothing follows `complete()` in the same expression (a CI check). A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`. This satisfies the GDD's "fresh `ctx.token`" guarantee without allocating; the GDD wording is amended (§ GDD sync).

154	### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty
155	
156	```gdscript
157	class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
158	enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
159	var phase: Phase
160	var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
161	func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
162	func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key is an opaque int; its layout is ADR-0004's
163	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
164	```
165	
166	The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.
167	
168	| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
169	|---|---|---|
170	| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
171	| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
172	| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
173	| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
174	| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
175	| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |

178	
179	`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. 181	### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback
182	
183	**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).
184	
185	- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
186	- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.
187	
188	**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3).
189	
190	**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.

192	**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. 339	- **Must** declare every kernel-invoked owner callable `-> CompletionToken` with `return ctx.complete()` as its **last** statement and nothing after `complete()` in that expression; **must never** declare one `-> void`, return a domain value, or use `assert()` or an engine error for control flow.

343	- **Must** return a status from every Class A mutator (`OK`, `REFUSED`, or `-code`) and deliver data through a caller-owned `out` object; **must** stop and `return ctx.complete()` at the first non-`OK` status, with no second `ctx.fault`.

### Implementation Guidelines
- **Must** register blocks, commands, hooks, fault domains and diagnostics channels only through `ModuleFacet.registrar` in `BOOTING`; **must never** register after the freeze.
- **Must** declare every kernel-invoked owner callable `-> CompletionToken` with `return ctx.complete()` as its **last** statement and nothing after `complete()` in that expression; **must never** declare one `-> void`, return a domain value, or use `assert()` or an engine error for control flow.
- **Must** report outcomes through `ctx` (`ok`/`reject`/`put`/`fault`); **must never** signal success or failure through the return value.
- **Must never** override a `CallContext` method in a subclass; subclasses only add methods.
- **Must** begin every mutator with `scope.open_for(<its block>)` and mark dirty keys with `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator; **must never** rely on a property setter for dirty tracking, and **must never** write a block outside a scope.
- **Must** return a status from every Class A mutator (`OK`, `REFUSED`, or `-code`) and deliver data through a caller-owned `out` object; **must** stop and `return ctx.complete()` at the first non-`OK` status, with no second `ctx.fault`.
- **Must** make `restore` copy into the existing block object; **must never** replace the block object a facade wraps.
- **Must** keep block objects `RefCounted` and plain-data; **must never** make a block a `Resource` or `Node`, or hand out a live container from a view.
- **Must** declare fault codes pre-packed in the owner's `*_faults.gd` with its static `DOMAIN_ID`; **must never** reuse or renumber a code.
- **Must** declare `tolerates_stale` on every `after` edge between hooks that do not always coincide.
- **Must** keep every hook allocation-free in steady state; **must** call kernel callables with `Callable.call()` and a fixed argument list, **never** `callv` on the hot path.
- **Must** drop references at teardown: in `SHUTTING_DOWN` the kernel clears every descriptor and `Callable` and owners drop their facets; a teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value.
- **Must never** let an owner callable subscribe to notifications (CR-10).

- A node whose `process_priority` is below `TICK_DRIVER` must be a registered INPUT_SURFACE object. Nothing else may run before the driver. Scene files (`.tscn`) must not set `process_priority` at all (the Inspector stores a literal); code sets it from `ProcessPriority`. A regex cannot see priorities set at runtime, so the authoritative check is a **boot-time tree walk**: every node whose priority is below `TICK_DRIVER` is a registered INPUT_SURFACE object, only `KernelHost` uses `TICK_DRIVER`'s value, and every INPUT_SURFACE, `KernelHost` and presentation node has the default (main-thread) `process_thread_group`, because a sub-thread group leaves the main-thread ordering and breaks the main-thread rule. Exactly which rules the lint tool can enforce statically and which move to boot walks is ADR-0010's call (OQ-16).
- No node other than `KernelHost` may use `TICK_DRIVER`'s value.
- A presentation node's `process_priority` is `PRESENTATION` or greater and is never set to a literal; it references the constant.
- **Main thread only (CR-1a).** The kernel, the driver and every owner callable run on the main thread.

- A **`ControlHandle`** carries the host-local control plane (§ 6). It is issued to Save/Load (`save_load`), the Chart Table's `PauseGate` (`pause_gate`) and the composition root (`game`); nobody else gets one.

- **SYSTEM-origin submission is not a handle.** `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key)` and `has_pending(type, dedupe_key)` are methods of the `HookContext` and `ApplyContext` objects the kernel passes into step hooks and `apply` (ADR-0003 defines the contexts). A SYSTEM command can therefore only be created inside a tick phase, by a registered owner, and never from a signal handler or `_process`. The test ingress (§ 8) is the one other caller.
- Handles are issued only while the kernel is `BOOTING` (like every registration, CR-6) and are not serialisable. Handle names are unique; a duplicate fails boot.

## ADR Dependencies

**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. After the call it clears the flag. A call made while the flag is set is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation; the MVP needs one context per kind, because a hook's `submit_system` queues and does not call another kernel callable synchronously.

-**The token check.** The kernel keeps one `CompletionToken` per context object. `complete()` sets `completed = true`, writes the current epoch into the token and returns it. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. Anything else, including `null`, a type default or a token kept from an earlier call, is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` (or, for a handler or a view callable, a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic without a fault). The check does not depend on what an aborted call returns (Verification 1). One hole is closed by rule: an owner that aborted *after* `complete()` ran would read as success, so `return ctx.complete()` is the **last statement** and nothing follows `complete()` in the same expression (a CI check). ### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty

- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.

-**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3).

+**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3). **Fail-closed never depends on an engine error aborting the callee** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review)*: a release build may log a script error and continue. It is carried by the explicit paths only — mutator status checks, `scope.fault` and the closed scope — with the `STRICT_DEBUG` checks and ADR-0004's debug-build missed-mark hash as backstops. An engine error that a release build swallows and that no mutator detects is outside what the kernel can see; KRN-CTX-06 documents it rather than claims it.

**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.
- **Must** declare fault codes pre-packed in the owner's `*_faults.gd` with its static `DOMAIN_ID`; **must never** reuse or renumber a code.
- **Must** declare `tolerates_stale` on every `after` edge between hooks that do not always coincide.
- **Must** keep every hook allocation-free in steady state; **must** call kernel callables with `Callable.call()` and a fixed argument list, **never** `callv` on the hot path.

-- **Must** drop references at teardown: in `SHUTTING_DOWN` the kernel clears every descriptor and `Callable` and owners drop their facets; a teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value.

+- **Must** keep owners alive explicitly: a registered `Callable` does **not** own its object (Verification 3), so the composition root holds every owner in one strong-reference list from `BOOTING` to `SHUTTING_DOWN`; boot checks every registered callable `is_valid()` after the freeze.

+- **Must** drop references at teardown: in `SHUTTING_DOWN` the kernel clears every descriptor and `Callable`, owners drop their facets and the composition root clears its owner list last; a teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value. The test starts from "callables do not own": an owner freed early shows up as an invalid callable at boot, not as a leak.

+- **Must never** use `await` in a kernel-invoked owner callable or anything it calls (a lint over `src/sim/` and `src/kernel/`): a suspended call returns a coroutine state (caught as `INCOMPLETE`) but could later resume against a re-armed context and scope and write through them. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review.)*
- **Must never** let an owner callable subscribe to notifications (CR-10).
## Alternatives Considered
- **A context is used re-entrantly.** Mitigation: the re-entrancy flag and `CONTEXT_REENTRY`.
- **An owner replaces its block object in `restore` and its facade goes stale.** Mitigation: the in-place rule and the restore-then-read facade test per block.
- **A reference cycle leaks at shutdown or between tests.** Mitigation: the `SHUTTING_DOWN` clear and the `OBJECT_COUNT` teardown test.
+- **An owner is freed while its callables are still registered** (callables hold only an id). Mitigation: the composition root's strong-reference list and the boot `is_valid()` check.
- **`registry_valid` is set wrongly.** Mitigation: set in one place; KRN-STATE-01 covers both kinds of `FAULTED`.
- **A facet leak gives presentation `SimViews` or a scope.** Mitigation: facets are issued by the composition root; a lint forbids `SimViews` and `WriteScope` in `src/presentation/`.
- **`C` exceeds the cap when a new divisor is added.** Mitigation: boot fails naming the divisor.

No code exists. Document changes: amend the kernel GDD (§ GDD sync); amend ADR-0002 so its result and control-outcome handlers take `(record, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken` and `register_command` is listed on the `BlockRegistrar` (done in the same pass as this ADR); amend `docs/architecture/architecture.md` § API Boundaries so `weld_join` returns a status and fills a caller-owned `WeldResult`, Class B mutators return `void`, and the `ReadViews`/`WriteScope` placeholders point here; change Derelict Authoring and Web Map wording that treats `STEP_BUDGET_MS` as a target (IC-4).
## Validation Criteria

-- On a **release export**: a callable that aborts yields `fault(INCOMPLETE)`; one returning a previous call's token yields `INCOMPLETE`; one returning the armed token with `completed` unset yields `INCOMPLETE`; a two-command batch on the reused context gives no spurious `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`.

+- On a **release export**: a callable that aborts yields `fault(INCOMPLETE)`; one returning a previous call's token yields `INCOMPLETE`; one returning the armed token with `completed` unset yields `INCOMPLETE`; one that hits `await` yields `INCOMPLETE` and never resumes into a later call's scope; the outcome for a callee that logs a script error and continues is recorded; a two-command batch on the reused context gives no spurious `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`.

- A mutator on a closed scope writes nothing, marks nothing, returns `REFUSED` and counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`; after a `scope.fault` later mutators in the same apply return `REFUSED` and nothing is counted twice; in `PAUSED_APPLY` `open_for` is false for blocks not in `writes_blocks`.
- A new game builds the MVP world through one `INIT` scope (Web Map `init_world` → Layout, Emitter, Interaction mutators) and delivers exactly one `ALL` batch per block on `LOADING → RUNNING`.
- A `validate` with no outcome is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`; a second outcome call is `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`; a re-entrant call is `CONTEXT_REENTRY`.

content.text:
I've fixed every engine problem the architecture review found, in 12 files. Nothing is committed yet.

**The two-argument `var_to_bytes` call.** Godot 4.7.2 won't compile it, so it now takes one argument everywhere it appeared:
- the three flagged GDDs (7 places in command-simulation-layer, 1 in ship-section-and-layout, 1 in suit-and-equipment)
- ADR-0002 (3 places) and `architecture.md`
- the traceability files, with TR-cmd-010 marked as revised today

The Suit GDD's 68-byte figure is still correct: the Item DB measured it with the one-argument form on 4.7.2, and the byte count adds up. Those three GDDs are back to Approved in the systems index, so all 26 MVP GDDs are Approved again.

**ADR-0003:**
- **Callables don't keep their objects alive** (HIGH, checked on the installed editor). The ADR now says the startup code must hold every owner in its own list. At boot, the kernel checks that each registered callable still points at a live object. The teardown test was rewritten on that basis.
- **Failing safely can't rely on the engine stopping the function** (MEDIUM). A release build may log a script error and keep going, so the ADR now relies only on its own fault paths, not on an abort. The release-export test now records which of the two behaviours actually happens.
- **`await` is banned** in any function the kernel calls, enforced by a lint. The kernel also checks the return value with `is_same()`, so a function that hit `await` is caught as incomplete.
- I removed the "if it exists" hedge on `get_argument_count()`; the method is there in 4.7.2.

**ADR-0001:**
- The boot check on which thread each node runs on now follows the default "inherit" setting up through the node's parents. Before, a node set to inherit under a background-thread parent would have passed.
- The clock lint now lists the real Godot 4 time functions. `OS.get_unix_time*` doesn't exist in Godot 4, so linting for it caught nothing. I also removed it from the Sanity GDD's lint list (AC-SN-130).

**ADR-0002:** the host's peer ID is now the engine constant `MultiplayerPeer.TARGET_PEER_SERVER` instead of a bare `1`.

**Still open:** one fix can't be confirmed without a release export. The test that records what a script error does in a release build has to run on an actual export. All three ADRs are still Proposed.

Say "commit and push" to commit these. After that, the next step is writing the Foundation ADRs with `/architecture-decision`: ADR-0007 (content pipeline) first, then ADR-0006 (save container), then ADR-0005 (determinism and hashing).
